To The Boys! Camping Committee, 
Montreal YeMeCeAe 


Gentlemens 


In spite of poor camping weather, the Boys' Camp had a near capacity 
registratione 


We were fortunate again in acquiring the able leadership of Mre Robert 
Kneeland, Mre William MacRae and Mre William Osterman, who are all veteran staff 
members of Camp Perrote With such highly skilled leadership and the return of 
half of the 1953 Counsellors, a successful eleventh year of operation was enjoyed 
by alle 


PROGRAM 
INTEREST GROUPS: A step forward in the Interest Groups program was the 


inclusion of staff members wivese Their leadership, 
particualrly in leatherwork, was a great boon to the programe 


Secondly, rather than following the established practice 
of limiting this program to the mornings, we held two crafts 
periodse Half the camp used the facilities in the morning 
and the remaining half used them in the afternoone This 
procedure doubled the use of the craft shop, 40 boys per day 
as against 20. Thus all but 20 boys in a 100 used the craft 
shop in a two week period, and as the average stay was 2e7 
weeks this year, we can assume that all campers got an 
opprotunity to use the shope 


This system also freed all other facilities on the 
camp for those who were not at craftse 


Other groups were: canoeing, braiding and knots, leatherwork, 
carving and archerye 


TRIPPING: Once again the Perrot war-canoes were in constant uses 

eee mee aes With the addition of another canoe donated by Kamp Kanawana, 
we were able to keep three canoes out,and one at camp for 
instructional purposese 


The water routes between Perrot and Carilon is so 
familiar to our older campers that much discussion centered 
around possible trips on the Ottawa River above the Carilon 
and Grenville locks. 


There were 16 canoe trips this year ranging from 2 to 
5 days each. Five boys of the Rangers totalled 14 days each. 


INDIAN COUNCIL The weekly meeting of the tribes proved as interesting 
FIRES : as evere Doug Smith, our Business Manager, joined the 


council with much enthusiasme In a great ceremony he was 
made blood-brother to Chief Black Bear (Bill MacRae) and 
was named Chief Three Arrowse 

Another totem pole was completed this yeare 


PERROT PENNY Fourteen different booths were made by the boys for 

CIRCUS : the faire Tho Wheel of Fortune, an Auction, Ping Pong 
Bounce Ball, Penny Toss and Soak you Pal were the most 
popular. 


Parents were invited and they seemed to enjoy the 
fair as much as the campers did. 


OTHER PROGRAM Other highlights were the Back woodsman Day, Backwards 
HIGHLIGHTS : Day, Indian Decathlon, Masquerade Birthday Party, Novelty 


Field Day, a play by the staff, Skit Nights, a movie, and 
finally the closing banquete 


On Sunday afternoons we held the usual swim meets, 
regattas, waterpolo tournaments and crafts displayse 


WATERFRONT The weather did not favour our swimming programe 
Even so 60 boysmssed YMCA Cards and 11 boyspassed from 
red cords (non-swimmer) to green cord (one lingth of the 
pool) 


HEALTH 


The health of the campers was goode Most cases were 
of a minor naturee There were two more serious cases; a 
recurrence of a dislocated knee during Boys’ camp and a 
sprained back during Girls' Campe 


Unfortunately the woight records were misplaced.» I 
am sure that with the improved menus, there would have been 
a corresponding improvement in the average gain in weight 
over last year's 35 pounds per camper.

The "Parliaments" was painted this Springe The 
dining hall floor and gallery were given their annual 
coatse The gallery of the hospital was also paintede 


The grougd around the dining hall was leveled 
which greatly enhances the appearance of this building. 


100 Spruce were transplanted from the back of the 
property to the area around the tentse 


Many of the 10,000 Spruce planted at the back of the 
camp have died or are so grown over that they cannot be 
found.e 


All broken windows were repaired this yeare 
All bunks were repaired and strengthened. 
All tie-rails were reenforceds 


The dining hall cesspool was emptied as the overflow 
was appearing on the surface againe 


A sound system with four l0inch speakers and an 
ampliphier was attached to our three-speed gramophone. 
We now have music with our mealse This systen was installed 
by Doug Smith, our Business Managere 


Industrial Caterers did an excellent job this summer. 
The stoves burned almost continuoulsy as will be verified 
by the increased gas billtt 


The new tuck system worked extremely well and greatly 
lessened the many headaches of the Business Managere 


RECOMMENDATIONS 


le Some thought should be given to staff living quarters 
other than the cottage which is the camp administration 
building. 


2. Some type of wash-house should replace the taps and mud- 
hole in the center of the camp.

4e

6 


Te 


Independent Grocers Alliance campers should not be 
accepted for periods less than two weekse They hardly 
had a chance to adjust themselves to camp life before 
their parents arrived ona visiting day, and took them 
homee Also, most of these campers were French-speaking 
and found it difficult to fit in with boys who had 
already been at camp for one or t wo weeks o 


All the dining hall tables need to be reenforcede 


The exterior of the dining hall will need painting 
next Springe 


The cesspool for the cottage needs to be emptied and 
the lines repaired as it now leaks back into the cottage 
basemente 


The wharves at the waterfront are beginning to break upe 
Some new ones will have to be constructed next Springe 
Possibly Mre OeNeH. Owen's suggestion of cement groins 
4s the solution to both the wharves and erosion problems. 


IN CLOSING 


I would like to thank Mre J. Ernest Millen for the bandsaw and his 
continued interest in the camps all members of the advanced and rear 
guards for their many hours of voluntary work; the staff and counsellors 
of the Boyst and Girls' Camp; the Boys’ Camping Committee; the Staff of 
The Montreal YMeC.A.; Miss Sheila Dover of the Camp Office and Mre Roy De 
Locke for their help in ensuring another successful season of campinge 


My sincere thanks, 


Respectfully submitted, 
Donald Cochrane, 
Directore
